newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Aug 19.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
DAILY TELEGRAPH
FEARS ON SMITH POWER VACUUM

WH Smith, the troubled retailing group, has issued a statement that it has no plans to de-merge. The group, which is due to report annual result later this month, denied it was under pressure from shareholders to de-merge. The comments come amid concern from institutional investors that WH Smith could tear itself apart as four internal candidates battle to take over as chief executive.
SAFEWAY TO RAISE PRICE WAR STAKES

Supermarket chain Safeway has launched a 20-million pound 'Price Protected' scheme, intensifying the price war between the main supermarkets. Under the scheme, any Safeway customer who can buy a product cheaper at Sainsbury's, Tesco or Asda will be offered either the product free or a full refund. The campaign will cover 650 of the most popular products at Safeway.
THE GUARDIAN
ARMANI SEEKS SLIMLINE LOOK

Italian fashion house Armani has announced plans for a restructuring which will create a new-look, slimline organisation via a series of mergers and spin-offs. According to the Ansa news agency, the changes may include the separation of the company's design activities from the rest of its businesses. The move is in line with changes at other Italian fashion firms, including Versace and Trussardi.
OFF-LICENCE CHAIN HITS BACK AT SUPERMARKETS

Off-licence chain Victoria Wine is set to unveil its first drinks superstore this weekend as it attempts to meet the challenge from supermarket wine departments. The first 'Martha's Vineyard' store will open in New Barnet, north London, on Saturday, at a site adjacent to a Tesco store. The company is specifically targeting new customers, including those who may currently buy their drinks at supermarkets.
LAURA ASHLEY SHUDDERS

Troubled fashion and home furnishings retailer Laura Ashley saw 10.7 million pounds wiped from its stock market value on Monday as investors anticipated a trading statement from the company this week. The statement is expected to contain a profits warning as well as possible job losses at Laura Ashley's Welsh factories. It is reported that the position of chief executive Ann Iverson is safe only because the board would find it difficult to replace her.
THE INDEPENDENT
CAMELOT'S RIVAL GETS THE GREEN LIGHT

A London court has ruled that '49s', a gambling game run by Britain's biggest bookmakers and which could rival the National Lottery, is legal. The case had been brought by Camelot, operators of the National Lottery, but the court ruled that the rival game was in fact a fixed-odds bet and not a lottery, and should therefore be allowed to continue. Camelot says it intends to appeal the decision.
BIOGLAN PHARMA PLANS 200M STG FLOAT NEXT YEAR

Pharmaceutical company Bioglan Pharma is planning a stock market flotation next year, although the company may not seek to raise any new money with the issue. Bioglan, now a drug delivery specialist, was incorporated in 1932 and has subsidiaries in five countries including Germany and the U.S. Chairman and chief executive Terry Sadler said the company would only seek to raise new money from the flotation if it were looking to make more acquisitions.
MERRYDOWN HIT BY DEPARTURE OF FINANCE CHIEF

Troubled cider group Merrydown, which suffered plummeting sales of its Two Dogs Lemonade product in the wake of the alcopops outcry, has lost its finance director just two months after the departure of its sales director. Stephen Burke is to be replaced in the post of finance director by his deputy, Michael Dinnis, while sales director Alan Rutherford, who left earlier this summer, is not to be replaced. Richard Pudgey, chairman and chief executive of the group, has so far survived the restructuring. BMC "44 171 377 1742
